title: The Overlook or the Water?
why: 2027 planning: contrasts the free overlook visit (the windshield nemesis) with the kayak tour, honest about weather.
hook_options: You saw Cave Point. Did you see the caves?
Overlook or kayak: what you actually get.
Most visitors see Cave Point from the wrong side.
caption: Most people see Cave Point from the overlook trail, snap a photo, and drive on. Here's what changes from a kayak. Do both if you can. Kayak tours return May 2027. #doorcounty #cavepoint #kayaking #lakemichigan

slides.headline: The overlook or the water?
slides.body: Most Cave Point visitors see it from the trail. Here's what changes when you see it from a kayak.

slides.headline: You see the top of the cliffs.
slides.body: Pretty, free, five minutes from the car. You're looking down at the water, not into the caves.

slides.headline: You see where the lake carved them.
slides.body: The caves and arches face the lake. The only way in is by boat.

slides.headline: The lot fills by mid-morning in July.
slides.body: It's small, and clear summer weekends pack it early.

slides.headline: 15 to 20 feet down, still clear.
slides.body: On calm days you watch the lakebed slide by under your seat.

slides.headline: Ten minutes, then the next stop.
slides.body: Most people take the photo and head back to the car.

slides.headline: Two hours along the shoreline.
slides.body: A guide picks the line, reads the wind, and calls the cave entry that morning.

slides.headline: The water has a weather veto.
slides.body: Wind and waves can move or cancel a tour. The overlook never cancels.

slides.headline: Overlook: free and fast. Water: the caves.
slides.body: Do both. Walk the overlook after your paddle and you'll know exactly where you were.

slides.headline: Kayak tours return May 2027.
slides.body: Book at doorcountykayaktours.com. Tag the friend who only did the overlook.
